topics_covered.title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.

• Linear Equations & Inequalities in 1 Variable: Form ax + b = 0 (solution x = -b/a). Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number REVERSES the inequality sign (e.g., -2x < 6 ⟹ x > -3). Solution sets expressed on real line or in interval notation.

• Systems of 2-Variable Linear Equations: ax + by = c and dx + ey = f. Solution methods: 1) Substitution; 2) Elimination; 3) Graphical intersection point (x, y). Consistent unique solution (intersecting lines), inconsistent no solution (parallel lines), dependent infinite solutions (coincident lines).
• Quadratic Equations: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Methods: Factoring, completing the square, and Quadratic Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
• Discriminant Analysis (Δ = b² - 4ac): If Δ > 0, two distinct real roots; If Δ = 0, one real repeated root (x = -b/(2a)); If Δ < 0, two complex conjugate roots (no real roots).
key_points: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.
topics_covered.explanation: Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.
topics_covered.diagram_illustration: Quadratic Discriminant Curve: Δ > 0 (Parabola crosses x-axis twice) ──> Δ = 0 (Parabola touches x-axis at vertex) ──> Δ < 0 (Parabola floats above/below x-axis).
topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Quadratic Discriminant Curve: Δ > 0 (Parabola crosses x-axis twice) ──> Δ = 0 (Parabola touches x-axis at vertex) ──> Δ < 0 (Parabola floats above/below x-axis).
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: Linear programming and break-even revenue models guide agricultural supply chain logistics and small-enterprise budgeting in Ethiopia.
topics_covered.exam_focus: High-yield EUEE questions: solving quadratic equations using discriminant, identifying values of k for which ax² + kx + c = 0 has a single repeated root (Δ = 0), and solving systems by elimination.
topics_covered.key_takeaway: Quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)]/(2a) yields exact roots; discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac dictates real root count.

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.
topics_covered.diagram_illustration: Function Mapping Machine: Input x ──> [Function f(x)] ──> Output y ──> [Inverse Function f⁻¹(y)] ──> Returns original x.
topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Function Mapping Machine: Input x ──> [Function f(x)] ──> Output y ──> [Inverse Function f⁻¹(y)] ──> Returns original x.
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: Economic demand-supply equilibrium models and commodity pricing curves in Ethiopia's ECX (Ethiopian Commodity Exchange) are modeled as inverse functions.
topics_covered.exam_focus: Very high frequency in EUEE: determining the domain of √(4 - x²), finding (f ∘ g)(3), and finding the remainder when a polynomial is divided by (x + 2).
topics_covered.key_takeaway: A function maps each input to a unique output; invertible functions must be one-to-one and symmetric across y = x.

topics_covered.title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Input-output Leontief economic models, network communication graphs, inventory tracking, and cryptography.
• Data Organization & Frequency Distributions: Discrete vs grouped frequency tables. Class intervals, lower/upper class boundaries, class mark (midpoint x = (L + U)/2), and cumulative frequency.

• Graphical Data Representations: Bar charts (discrete categories, gaps between bars); Histograms (continuous data, bars touch, bar area proportional to frequency); Pie charts (circular sectors, sector angle = (f / N) × 360°).

• Measures of Central Tendency: 1) Mean x̄ = (Σ x) / n or x̄ = (Σ f·x) / (Σ f); 2) Median: Middle score when data is ordered (for even n, average of two middle terms); 3) Mode: Most frequently occurring score (unimodal, bimodal, or no mode).
• Basic Probability Concepts: Sample space S (all possible outcomes), Event E (subset of S). Theoretical Probability P(E) = n(E) / n(S) where 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1. Complementary Event: P(E') = 1 - P(E).
key_points: In a histogram, bars MUST touch because data is continuous; in a bar chart, gaps separate discrete categories.
The sum of sector angles in a pie chart is ALWAYS 360°.
Probability is strictly bounded: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 (0 = impossible event, 1 = certain event).
topics_covered.explanation: Statistics and probability provide tools for analyzing data and quantifying uncertainty. Descriptive statistics condense large data sets into summary averages and charts, while probability models chance events.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Statistics and probability provide tools for analyzing data and quantifying uncertainty. Descriptive statistics condense large data sets into summary averages and charts, while probability models chance events.

topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Data Central Tendency Distributions: Symmetric Distribution (Mean = Median = Mode) ──> Positively Skewed (Mode < Median < Mean) ──> Negatively Skewed (Mean < Median < Mode).
topics_covered.ethiopian_context: Agricultural crop yield forecasting and national health epidemic tracking by the Ethiopian Public Health Institute rely on statistical measures and probability models.
topics_covered.exam_focus: High-frequency EUEE questions: calculating mean of grouped frequency data, calculating pie chart sector angles, finding median from cumulative frequency, and calculating basic event probabilities.
topics_covered.key_takeaway: Mean x̄ = Σ(f·x)/N; Median is middle value; Mode is most frequent; Probability P(E) = n(E)/n(S) where 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1.

euee_exam_tips.trap: Extraneous Solutions After Squaring
euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Always plug every candidate answer back into the ORIGINAL equation! If x = -2 results in √(-2) or a negative value equal to a square root, it must be discarded.

euee_exam_tips.trap: Multiplying an Inequality by a Negative Variable
euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Never multiply both sides of an inequality by an unknown variable x unless you partition the problem into positive and negative cases. Use sign charts (critical value method) instead!

euee_exam_tips.trap: Vieta's Shortcut for Multiple Choice
euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Before solving lengthy quadratics, check if any option matches sum = -b/a and product = c/a. This often answers the question in under 15 seconds.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

quick_example.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
quick_example.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
quick_example.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.topic_title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Dimensions (rows x columns), entries, row vectors, column vectors, square matrices, and equality of matrices.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 3.2 Matrix Operations: Addition, Scalar & Multiplication
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Commutative/associative properties of addition, scalar distribution, row-column dot product multiplication criteria.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 3.4 Elementary Row Operations and Gaussian Elimination
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.4 Elementary Row Operations and Gaussian Elimination
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Row swapping, scalar multiplication of rows, row replacement, and reducing to row-echelon form.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.
topics_covered.explanation: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.
topics_covered.diagram_illustration:
[Diagram: Vector Representation in Polar and Cartesian Systems]
• Polar Coordinates (R, θ): Vector specified by scalar magnitude R = |A⃗| and counterclockwise angle θ from the positive x-axis.
• Cartesian Components (Ax, Ay): Vector resolved into orthogonal components where Ax = |A⃗| cos θ and Ay = |A⃗| sin θ.
• Unit Vector Form: A⃗ = Ax î + Ay ĵ
• Magnitude Formula: |A⃗| = √(Ax² + Ay²)
• Direction Angle: θ = arctan(Ay / Ax)
• Vector Representation: Tail at origin (0,0), head pointing at (Ax, Ay).
topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Vector Component Resolution: Vector v at angle θ ──> Horizontal Component v_x = ||v|| cos θ ──> Vertical Component v_y = ||v|| sin θ. Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²).

practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

topics_covered.title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Input-output Leontief economic models, network communication graphs, inventory tracking, and cryptography.
• Data Organization & Frequency Distributions: Discrete vs grouped frequency tables. Class intervals, lower/upper class boundaries, class mark (midpoint x = (L + U)/2), and cumulative frequency.

• Graphical Data Representations: Bar charts (discrete categories, gaps between bars); Histograms (continuous data, bars touch, bar area proportional to frequency); Pie charts (circular sectors, sector angle = (f / N) × 360°).

• Measures of Central Tendency: 1) Mean x̄ = (Σ x) / n or x̄ = (Σ f·x) / (Σ f); 2) Median: Middle score when data is ordered (for even n, average of two middle terms); 3) Mode: Most frequently occurring score (unimodal, bimodal, or no mode).
• Basic Probability Concepts: Sample space S (all possible outcomes), Event E (subset of S). Theoretical Probability P(E) = n(E) / n(S) where 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1. Complementary Event: P(E') = 1 - P(E).
key_points: In a histogram, bars MUST touch because data is continuous; in a bar chart, gaps separate discrete categories.
The sum of sector angles in a pie chart is ALWAYS 360°.
Probability is strictly bounded: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 (0 = impossible event, 1 = certain event).

quick_example.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
quick_example.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
quick_example.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.1 Concepts of a Matrix and Matrix Notations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Dimensions (rows x columns), entries, row vectors, column vectors, square matrices, and equality of matrices.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.
topics_covered.explanation: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.

topics_covered.title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.5 Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Augmented matrices, consistent vs. inconsistent systems, unique solutions, infinitely many solutions, and geometric interpretation.

• Linear Equations & Inequalities in 1 Variable: Form ax + b = 0 (solution x = -b/a). Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number REVERSES the inequality sign (e.g., -2x < 6 ⟹ x > -3). Solution sets expressed on real line or in interval notation.

• Systems of 2-Variable Linear Equations: ax + by = c and dx + ey = f. Solution methods: 1) Substitution; 2) Elimination; 3) Graphical intersection point (x, y). Consistent unique solution (intersecting lines), inconsistent no solution (parallel lines), dependent infinite solutions (coincident lines).
• Quadratic Equations: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Methods: Factoring, completing the square, and Quadratic Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
• Discriminant Analysis (Δ = b² - 4ac): If Δ > 0, two distinct real roots; If Δ = 0, one real repeated root (x = -b/(2a)); If Δ < 0, two complex conjugate roots (no real roots).
key_points: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.
topics_covered.explanation: Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.

topics_covered.title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.6 Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Invertibility condition, Gauss-Jordan elimination [A | I] -> [I | A^-1], and solving AX = B via X = A^-1 B.
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.
topics_covered.detailed_explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

topics_covered.illustration_analogy: Function Mapping Machine: Input x ──> [Function f(x)] ──> Output y ──> [Inverse Function f⁻¹(y)] ──> Returns original x.

topics_covered.key_takeaway: A function maps each input to a unique output; invertible functions must be one-to-one and symmetric across y = x.

topics_covered.title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.7 Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Input-output Leontief economic models, network communication graphs, inventory tracking, and cryptography.
• Data Organization & Frequency Distributions: Discrete vs grouped frequency tables. Class intervals, lower/upper class boundaries, class mark (midpoint x = (L + U)/2), and cumulative frequency.

• Graphical Data Representations: Bar charts (discrete categories, gaps between bars); Histograms (continuous data, bars touch, bar area proportional to frequency); Pie charts (circular sectors, sector angle = (f / N) × 360°).

• Measures of Central Tendency: 1) Mean x̄ = (Σ x) / n or x̄ = (Σ f·x) / (Σ f); 2) Median: Middle score when data is ordered (for even n, average of two middle terms); 3) Mode: Most frequently occurring score (unimodal, bimodal, or no mode).
• Basic Probability Concepts: Sample space S (all possible outcomes), Event E (subset of S). Theoretical Probability P(E) = n(E) / n(S) where 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1. Complementary Event: P(E') = 1 - P(E).
key_points: In a histogram, bars MUST touch because data is continuous; in a bar chart, gaps separate discrete categories.
The sum of sector angles in a pie chart is ALWAYS 360°.
Probability is strictly bounded: 0 ≤ P(E) ≤ 1 (0 = impossible event, 1 = certain event).
topics_covered.explanation: Statistics and probability provide tools for analyzing data and quantifying uncertainty. Descriptive statistics condense large data sets into summary averages and charts, while probability models chance events.

euee_exam_tips.trap: Extraneous Solutions After Squaring
euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Always plug every candidate answer back into the ORIGINAL equation! If x = -2 results in √(-2) or a negative value equal to a square root, it must be discarded.

euee_exam_tips.trap: Multiplying an Inequality by a Negative Variable
euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Never multiply both sides of an inequality by an unknown variable x unless you partition the problem into positive and negative cases. Use sign charts (critical value method) instead!

euee_exam_tips.trap: Vieta's Shortcut for Multiple Choice
euee_exam_tips.how_to_avoid: Before solving lengthy quadratics, check if any option matches sum = -b/a and product = c/a. This often answers the question in under 15 seconds.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.

quick_example.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
quick_example.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
quick_example.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_matrix_operation.detailed_overview:
Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.

Key Takeaway: Vectors have magnitude ||v|| = √(x²+y²) and direction θ; component form v = v_x i + v_y j allows simple component-wise operations.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Aviation flight path vector navigation by Ethiopian Airlines pilots accounts for crosswind velocity vectors over the Horn of Africa.

topics_covered.title: 3.x Matrix Operations: Addition, Scalar & Multiplication
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic: Matrix Operations: Addition, Scalar & Multiplication

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.

• Polar Coordinates (R, θ): Vector specified by scalar magnitude R = |A⃗| and counterclockwise angle θ from the positive x-axis.
• Cartesian Components (Ax, Ay): Vector resolved into orthogonal components where Ax = |A⃗| cos θ and Ay = |A⃗| sin θ.

• Magnitude Formula: |A⃗| = √(Ax² + Ay²)
• Direction Angle: θ = arctan(Ay / Ax)
• Vector Representation: Tail at origin (0,0), head pointing at (Ax, Ay).

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_systems_of_linea.detailed_overview:
Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.

Key Takeaway: Quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)]/(2a) yields exact roots; discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac dictates real root count.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Linear programming and break-even revenue models guide agricultural supply chain logistics and small-enterprise budgeting in Ethiopia.

topics_covered.title: 3.x Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.x Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic: Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables

• Linear Equations & Inequalities in 1 Variable: Form ax + b = 0 (solution x = -b/a). Multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number REVERSES the inequality sign (e.g., -2x < 6 ⟹ x > -3). Solution sets expressed on real line or in interval notation.

• Systems of 2-Variable Linear Equations: ax + by = c and dx + ey = f. Solution methods: 1) Substitution; 2) Elimination; 3) Graphical intersection point (x, y). Consistent unique solution (intersecting lines), inconsistent no solution (parallel lines), dependent infinite solutions (coincident lines).
• Quadratic Equations: Standard form ax² + bx + c = 0 (a ≠ 0). Methods: Factoring, completing the square, and Quadratic Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
• Discriminant Analysis (Δ = b² - 4ac): If Δ > 0, two distinct real roots; If Δ = 0, one real repeated root (x = -b/(2a)); If Δ < 0, two complex conjugate roots (no real roots).
key_points: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Algebraic equations and inequalities model balanced quantities and constraints. Linear systems resolve simultaneous conditions, while quadratic equations analyze parabolic trajectories and maximum/minimum optimization problems.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Curriculum topic: Systems of Linear Equations with Two and Three Variables

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Key Principle**: Reversing the inequality sign when dividing by a negative number is mandatory.
- **Key Principle**: Extraneous roots must be checked whenever denominators contain variables.
- **Key Principle**: Discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac instantly reveals the number and nature of quadratic roots without full solving.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**
```text
Quadratic Discriminant Curve: Δ > 0 (Parabola crosses x-axis twice) ──> Δ = 0 (Parabola touches x-axis at vertex) ──> Δ < 0 (Parabola floats above/below x-axis).
```

| **Examination Traps** | High-yield EUEE questions: solving quadratic equations using discriminant, ident... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Linear programming and break-even revenue models guide agricultural supply chain logistics and small-enterprise budgeting in Ethiopia.

### 5. EUEE Entrance Examination Strategy & Examiner Distractors
High-yield EUEE questions: solving quadratic equations using discriminant, identifying values of k for which ax² + kx + c = 0 has a single repeated root (Δ = 0), and solving systems by elimination.

### 6. Comprehensive Student Takeaway
Quadratic formula x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)]/(2a) yields exact roots; discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac dictates real root count.

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_inverse_of_a_squ.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations (Unit 3: Unit 3: Core Syllabus Concepts). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_inverse_of_a_squ.detailed_overview:
Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

Key Takeaway: A function maps each input to a unique output; invertible functions must be one-to-one and symmetric across y = x.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Economic demand-supply equilibrium models and commodity pricing curves in Ethiopia's ECX (Ethiopian Commodity Exchange) are modeled as inverse functions.

topics_covered.title: 3.x Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.x Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic: Inverse of a Square Matrix and Matrix Equations
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).

book-11-math_ch_3_topic_applications_of_.unit_summary: Core Study Notes & Illustrated Breakdown for Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business (Unit 3: Unit 3: Core Syllabus Concepts). Prepared according to the Ethiopian Grade 11 (General) Mathematics syllabus.
book-11-math_ch_3_topic_applications_of_.detailed_overview:
Trigonometry translates angular rotation into linear coordinates. The unit circle extends trigonometric functions beyond acute right-triangle geometry into periodic wave functions modeling sound, alternating current, and planetary orbits.

Key Takeaway: The Pythagorean identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and the unit circle define all trigonometric transformations.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Trigonometric triangulation is used by the Ethiopian Geospatial Information Institute for topological elevation mapping of the Semien and Bale mountain ranges.

topics_covered.title: 3.x Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
topics_covered.topic_title: 3.x Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic: Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

Trigonometry translates angular rotation into linear coordinates. The unit circle extends trigonometric functions beyond acute right-triangle geometry into periodic wave functions modeling sound, alternating current, and planetary orbits.

Key Takeaway: The Pythagorean identity sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 and the unit circle define all trigonometric transformations.

Ethiopian Context & Real-World Application: Trigonometric triangulation is used by the Ethiopian Geospatial Information Institute for topological elevation mapping of the Semien and Bale mountain ranges.

topics_covered.topic_title: 3.x Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Curriculum topic: Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

### 1. Theoretical Foundations & Governing Principles
Trigonometry translates angular rotation into linear coordinates. The unit circle extends trigonometric functions beyond acute right-triangle geometry into periodic wave functions modeling sound, alternating current, and planetary orbits.

**Curriculum Syllabus Alignment:** Curriculum topic: Applications of Matrices in Networks and Business

### 2. Systematic Concept Breakdown & Mechanisms
- **Periodicity**: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
- **Key Principle**: Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
- **Key Principle**: Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

### 3. Core Reference Table & Visual Schema
**Visual / Experimental Schema:**

Unit Circle Quadrants (ASTC): Q2 [Sin +] | Q1 [All +] ────────┼──────── Q3 [Tan +] | Q4 [Cos +] ("All Students Take Chemistry").

| **Examination Traps** | High-frequency EUEE questions: solving trig equations like 2 cos²x - cos x - 1 =... | Critical EUEE Target Point |

### 4. Real-World Ethiopian Application & Technological Context
Trigonometric triangulation is used by the Ethiopian Geospatial Information Institute for topological elevation mapping of the Semien and Bale mountain ranges.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Formula det(A) = ad - bc, geometric interpretation as signed area of parallelogram formed by row vectors.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.
topics_covered.explanation: Vectors represent directional physical quantities. Decomposing vectors into orthogonal x and y components transforms complex 2D vector addition into simple scalar arithmetic along independent coordinate axes.

topics_covered.title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Cofactor matrix, classical adjoint adj(A) = C^T, and inversion formula A^-1 = (1/det(A)) adj(A).
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

topics_covered.title: 4.6 Applications of Determinants in Geometry
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Area of triangles via coordinates, collinearity test of three points, and equation of lines through two points.

• Angles & Parallel Lines: Transversal intersecting two parallel lines forms: 1) Corresponding angles (equal); 2) Alternate interior angles (equal); 3) Alternate exterior angles (equal); 4) Consecutive interior angles (supplementary, sum = 180°).

• Triangle Congruence & Similarity: Congruent triangles (identical shape and size) criteria: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS. Similar triangles (same shape, proportional sides) criteria: AA, SSS similarity, SAS similarity. Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (scale factor k)².⏹

• Pythagorean Theorem & Special Right Triangles: In right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c: a² + b² = c². Special triangles: 1) 45°-45°-90° triangle (sides x : x : x√2); 2) 30°-60°-90° triangle (sides x : x√3 : 2x).

• Quadrilaterals & Polygons: Parallelogram (opposite sides/angles equal, diagonals bisect); Rectangle (right angles, equal diagonals); Rhombus (perpendicular diagonals); Square (all sides/angles equal). Polygon interior angle sum = (n - 2) × 180°; Exterior angle sum = 360°.
key_points: Consecutive interior angles along a transversal are supplementary (sum = 180°), NOT equal.
Similarity ratio k implies perimeter ratio k, but area ratio k².
The hypotenuse of a 30°-60°-90° triangle is twice the length of the side opposite the 30° angle.
topics_covered.explanation: Plane geometry analyzes spatial relationships, angle properties, and structural forms. Congruence and similarity enable indirect distance measurement, while the Pythagorean theorem provides the geometric link between distance and coordinate algebra.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 4.1 Determinants of 2x2 Matrices
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Formula det(A) = ad - bc, geometric interpretation as signed area of parallelogram formed by row vectors.

• Scalars vs Vectors: Scalar quantity has magnitude only (mass, temperature, speed, energy). Vector quantity has BOTH magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force, acceleration). Directed line segment representation AB.

• 2D Vector Component Form: Vector v in Cartesian plane: v = (v_x, v_y) = v_x i + v_y j, where i = (1, 0) and j = (0, 1) are standard unit vectors along x and y axes. Components: v_x = ||v|| cos θ, v_y = ||v|| sin θ.
• Magnitude & Direction Angle: Magnitude ||v|| = √(v_x² + v_y²). Direction angle θ = tan⁻¹(v_y / v_x) (quadrant adjusted). Unit vector u in direction of v: u = v / ||v||.

• Vector Operations: Vector addition u + v = (u_x + v_x, u_y + v_y) (Triangle / Parallelogram Law). Scalar multiplication k·v = (k·v_x, k·v_y). Dot product u · v = u_x v_x + u_y v_y = ||u|| ||v|| cos θ.
key_points: Magnitude of a vector is always a non-negative scalar ||v|| ≥ 0.
A unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1: ||u|| = 1.
Two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular) if and only if their dot product is zero: u · v = 0.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Solving Rational Equation with Extraneous Root Check
worked_examples.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!
worked_examples.result: Solution Set: S = {1}. Note: x = 3 is strictly excluded by domain restrictions.
worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

topics_covered.title: 4.4 Adjoint Matrix and Inverse Calculation
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Cofactor matrix, classical adjoint adj(A) = C^T, and inversion formula A^-1 = (1/det(A)) adj(A).
• Relation vs Function: A relation is a set of ordered pairs (x, y). A function is a relation where each domain element x is mapped to EXACTLY ONE range element y (passes Vertical Line Test).
• Domain & Range Restrictions: Exclude values that make denominators zero (f(x) = 1/x ⇒ x ≠ 0) or radicands of even roots negative (f(x) = √(x - 3) ⇒ x ≥ 3).
• Function Composition: (f ∘ g)(x) = f(g(x)). Domain of (f ∘ g) requires x to be in the domain of g, and g(x) to be in the domain of f.
• Inverse Functions (f⁻¹): Exists if and only if f is one-to-one (bijective, passes Horizontal Line Test). Graph of f⁻¹ is the reflection of f across the diagonal line y = x.
• Polynomial Theorems: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - c), the remainder is P(c). Factor Theorem: (x - c) is a factor of P(x) if and only if P(c) = 0.
key_points: To find the inverse algebraically: swap x and y, then solve for y: y = f⁻¹(x).
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x and f⁻¹(f(x)) = x for all valid domain values.
A polynomial of degree n has at most n complex roots (Fundamental Theorem of Algebra).
topics_covered.explanation: Functions establish deterministic mathematical relationships. Finding inverses allows reversing processes, while polynomial division theorems eliminate trial-and-error factoring of cubic and quartic equations.

quick_example.problem: Solve the rational equation for x: [ (2x) / (x - 3) ] - [ 6 / (x - 3) ] = x + 1.
quick_example.step_solution:
Step 1: Identify domain restriction: Denominator x - 3 ≠ 0 => x ≠ 3.
Step 2: Combine fractions on left side with common denominator: (2x - 6)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 3: Factor the numerator: 2(x - 3)/(x - 3) = x + 1.
Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 4.5 Cramer Rule for Linear Systems
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Determinant quotient formula xi = det(Ai)/det(A) for non-singular square systems and solvability checks.
• Primary Trigonometric Ratios (Right Triangle): sin θ = Opp/Hyp, cos θ = Adj/Hyp, tan θ = Opp/Adj (SOH-CAH-TOA). Reciprocals: csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, cot θ = 1/tan θ.

• Unit Circle & Radians: Coordinates of point on unit circle (r = 1): (x, y) = (cos θ, sin θ). Angle conversion: π radians = 180°. Quadrant signs (ASTC rule): All positive in Q1, Sin in Q2, Tan in Q3, Cos in Q4.
• Fundamental Pythagorean Identities: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.
• Addition & Double-Angle Formulas: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; sin(2θ) = 2 sin θ cos θ; cos(2θ) = cos²θ - sin²θ = 2cos²θ - 1 = 1 - 2sin²θ.
• Laws of Sines & Cosines (Any Triangle): Law of Sines: a / sin A = b / sin B = c / sin C = 2R. Law of Cosines: c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C.
key_points: Periodicity: sin θ and cos θ repeat every 2π radians (360°); tan θ repeats every π radians (180°).
Use the Law of Cosines when two sides and the included angle (SAS) or all three sides (SSS) are known.
Always check for the ambiguous case (two possible triangles) when using the Law of Sines with SSA.

topics_covered.title: 4.6 Applications of Determinants in Geometry
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Area of triangles via coordinates, collinearity test of three points, and equation of lines through two points.

• Angles & Parallel Lines: Transversal intersecting two parallel lines forms: 1) Corresponding angles (equal); 2) Alternate interior angles (equal); 3) Alternate exterior angles (equal); 4) Consecutive interior angles (supplementary, sum = 180°).

• Triangle Congruence & Similarity: Congruent triangles (identical shape and size) criteria: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS. Similar triangles (same shape, proportional sides) criteria: AA, SSS similarity, SAS similarity. Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (scale factor k)².⏹

• Pythagorean Theorem & Special Right Triangles: In right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c: a² + b² = c². Special triangles: 1) 45°-45°-90° triangle (sides x : x : x√2); 2) 30°-60°-90° triangle (sides x : x√3 : 2x).

• Quadrilaterals & Polygons: Parallelogram (opposite sides/angles equal, diagonals bisect); Rectangle (right angles, equal diagonals); Rhombus (perpendicular diagonals); Square (all sides/angles equal). Polygon interior angle sum = (n - 2) × 180°; Exterior angle sum = 360°.
key_points: Consecutive interior angles along a transversal are supplementary (sum = 180°), NOT equal.
Similarity ratio k implies perimeter ratio k, but area ratio k².
The hypotenuse of a 30°-60°-90° triangle is twice the length of the side opposite the 30° angle.

Step 4: For x ≠ 3, cancel (x - 3): 2 = x + 1 => x = 1.
Step 5: Verify x = 1 in original equation: LHS = 2(1)/(-2) - 6/(-2) = -1 + 3 = 2. RHS = 1 + 1 = 2. Valid!

worked_examples.examiner_note: EUEE examiners often include x = 3 as option A to catch students who cancel terms without domain checking!

worked_examples.title: Worked Example: Finding Maximum/Minimum Value using Vertex Formula
worked_examples.problem: A projectile's path is modeled by the function h(t) = -5t² + 30t + 2, where h is height in meters and t is time in seconds. Find the maximum height and the time taken to reach it.
worked_examples.step_solution:
Step 1: The quadratic function h(t) = at² + bt + c has a = -5, b = 30, c = 2.
Step 2: Since a < 0, the parabola opens downwards, so the vertex represents the maximum.
Step 3: Time at vertex t = -b / (2a) = -30 / [2(-5)] = -30 / -10 = 3 seconds.
Step 4: Evaluate h(3): h(3) = -5(3)² + 30(3) + 2 = -5(9) + 90 + 2 = -45 + 90 + 2 = 47 meters.
worked_examples.result: Maximum height is 47 meters, reached at t = 3 seconds.
worked_examples.examiner_note: Remember that the axis of symmetry x = -b/(2a) gives the time, while f(-b/(2a)) gives the maximum value itself.

practice_quiz.question: What is the solution set of the equation √(3x + 1) = x - 3 in the real numbers?
practice_quiz.explanation: Squaring both sides gives 3x + 1 = (x - 3)² = x² - 6x + 9 => x² - 9x + 8 = 0 => (x - 8)(x - 1) = 0. Roots are x = 8 and x = 1. Testing x = 1: √(4) = 2, but 1 - 3 = -2 (2 ≠ -2, extraneous!). Testing x = 8: √(25) = 5, and 8 - 3 = 5 (Valid!). Thus S = {8}.

practice_quiz.question: If the quadratic equation 3x² - kx + 12 = 0 has equal real roots, what are the possible values of k?
practice_quiz.explanation: Equal real roots require discriminant Δ = b² - 4ac = 0. Here (-k)² - 4(3)(12) = 0 => k² - 144 = 0 => k² = 144 => k = ±12.

topics_covered.title: 4.6 Applications of Determinants in Geometry
short_notes: • Curriculum Focus: Area of triangles via coordinates, collinearity test of three points, and equation of lines through two points.

• Angles & Parallel Lines: Transversal intersecting two parallel lines forms: 1) Corresponding angles (equal); 2) Alternate interior angles (equal); 3) Alternate exterior angles (equal); 4) Consecutive interior angles (supplementary, sum = 180°).

• Triangle Congruence & Similarity: Congruent triangles (identical shape and size) criteria: SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS, RHS. Similar triangles (same shape, proportional sides) criteria: AA, SSS similarity, SAS similarity. Ratio of areas of similar triangles = (scale factor k)².⏹

• Pythagorean Theorem & Special Right Triangles: In right triangle with legs a, b and hypotenuse c: a² + b² = c². Special triangles: 1) 45°-45°-90° triangle (sides x : x : x√2); 2) 30°-60°-90° triangle (sides x : x√3 : 2x).

• Quadrilaterals & Polygons: Parallelogram (opposite sides/angles equal, diagonals bisect); Rectangle (right angles, equal diagonals); Rhombus (perpendicular diagonals); Square (all sides/angles equal). Polygon interior angle sum = (n - 2) × 180°; Exterior angle sum = 360°.
key_points: Consecutive interior angles along a transversal are supplementary (sum = 180°), NOT equal.
Similarity ratio k implies perimeter ratio k, but area ratio k².
The hypotenuse of a 30°-60°-90° triangle is twice the length of the side opposite the 30° angle.
